source.text: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν πάλιν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης τῆς Τιβεριάδος· ἐφανέρωσεν δὲ οὕτως.

records.literal_gloss: After these things revealed himself again the Jesus to the disciples at the sea of the Tiberias; he revealed now thus.

en.L: After these things Jesus revealed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} again to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} revealed [{{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}] in this way.
en.B: After this Jesus revealed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to the disciples once more, by the Sea of Tiberias. It happened in this way.
en.R: Later, Jesus showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to the disciples again. It was beside the Sea of Tiberias, which is another name for the Sea of Galilee. This is how it happened.

fr.L: Après ces choses, Jésus se manifesta de nouveau aux disciples au bord de la mer de Tibériade ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se manifesta ainsi.
fr.B: Après cela, Jésus se manifesta encore aux disciples, au bord de la mer de Tibériade. Voici comment cela se passa.
fr.R: Plus tard, Jésus s’est montré de nouveau aux disciples. C’était au bord de la mer de Tibériade, qu’on appelle aussi la mer de Galilée. Voici comment cela s’est passé.

vi.L: Sau những điều này, Đức Giê-xu lại tỏ mình ra cho các môn đồ tại biển Ti-bê-ri-át; và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tỏ [mình ra] như thế này.
vi.B: Sau đó, Đức Giê-xu lại tỏ mình ra cho các môn đồ, bên bờ biển Ti-bê-ri-át. Việc xảy ra như sau.
vi.R: Ít lâu sau, Đức Giê-xu lại hiện ra cho các môn đồ thấy. Lần này là ở bên bờ biển Ti-bê-ri-át, cũng gọi là biển Ga-li-lê. Chuyện xảy ra như thế này.

ko.L: 이 일들 후에 예수께서 디베랴 바닷가에서 제자들에게 다시 자신을 나타내셨는데, 이렇게 나타내셨다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 예수께서 디베랴 바닷가에서 제자들에게 다시 자신을 나타내셨다. 그 일은 이렇게 일어났다.
ko.R: 얼마 뒤에 예수께서 다시 제자들에게 모습을 보이셨다. 디베랴 호숫가에서였다. 디베랴 호수는 갈릴리 호수의 다른 이름이다. 그 일은 이렇게 일어났다.

decisions.choice: revealed himself: made himself known, showed himself openly
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring into the open what was hidden. John used it of the glory Jesus revealed at Cana (2:11) and of his being revealed to Israel (1:31). Here the risen Jesus shows himself to his disciples when and as he chooses; at first they do not know him (verse 4). The same verb opens this story and closes it (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the Sea of Tiberias: the lake of Galilee
decisions.reason: John gave both names for the lake at 6:1; here he uses only the newer one, taken from the city of Tiberias that Herod Antipas built on its western shore. The scene has moved from Jerusalem back to Galilee, where several of the disciples came from and where some of them had been fishermen (Mark 1:16-20).

decisions.choice: After these things: a loose link back to the appearances of chapter 20
decisions.reason: John often moves to a new episode with this phrase and gives no length of time (5:1; 6:1; 7:1). The words of 20:30-31 read like the close of the book, since they state why it was written; chapter 21 follows them with one more appearance and a second closing (21:24-25), so it may be read as an epilogue to the Gospel. No known manuscript of John ends at 20:31.

decisions.choice: revealed (L, B); showed (R); It happened in this way (B); This is how it happened (R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:11, Literal and Balanced say "revealed" and Readable the plainer "showed". The short second clause introduces the story that follows, so Balanced and Readable turn it into a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: which is another name for the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Readable tells the reader that this is the lake of chapter 6 under its other name (meaning decision m2), as Readable did at 6:1.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("il dit", "ils voient", "Jésus vient"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (21:1-14). The passé simple ("se manifesta", "ils sortirent") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (21:3 "ils lui disent", 21:9 "ils voient", 21:13 "Jésus vient, et il prend"), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus s'est montré"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("vous avez pris").

decisions.choice: se manifesta (L, B); s'est montré (R); the reflexive "se" without the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use "manifester", as for the same verb at 1:31 and 2:11, and Readable the plainer "se montrer" (meaning decision m1). French says "himself" with the reflexive "se", which is never capitalised, so the span the English puts on "himself" has no French counterpart here, as with "ne se confiait pas" at 2:24; Literal's "il" in the second clause carries the setting.

decisions.choice: "tỏ mình ra" (L, B); "hiện ra cho ... thấy" (R)
decisions.reason: "tỏ mình ra" keeps the sense of making himself known; Readable uses the everyday word for an appearance.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} for Jesus in the narrative; "Ngài" written plainly at the start of a sentence
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the whole book; only the capital changes.

decisions.choice: "디베랴 바다" (L, B); "디베랴 호수", explained as the Sea of Galilee (R)
decisions.reason: "디베랴 바다" is the established Korean name and keeps the Greek word "sea"; Readable calls it a lake, which is what it is, and names it as the Sea of Galilee as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean ("자신", "께서", the honorific -시-), through 21:1-14
alternatives: deity_pronoun spans as in the English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7); respect for Jesus is carried by "께서", the honorific -시- and "그분" at every level. Recorded once for this passage.

source.text: ἦσαν ὁμοῦ Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ Θωμᾶς ὁ λεγόμενος Δίδυμος καὶ Ναθαναὴλ ὁ ἀπὸ Κανὰ τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ οἱ τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ ἄλλοι ἐκ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ δύο.

records.literal_gloss: Were together Simon Peter and Thomas the [one] being called Didymus and Nathanael the [one] from Cana of the Galilee and the [ones] of the Zebedee and others of the disciples of him two.

en.L: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas, the [one] called Didymus, and Nathanael, the [one] from Cana of Galilee, and the [sons] of Zebedee, and two others of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.B: Simon Peter was there with Thomas (called Didymus, which means Twin), Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, Zebedee's sons, and two more of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.R: Some of the disciples were together. Simon Peter was there, and Thomas, who was called the Twin. Nathanael was there too. He came from the town of Cana in Galilee. The sons of Zebedee were there, and two other disciples of Jesus.

fr.L: Il y avait ensemble Simon Pierre, et Thomas, [celui] appelé Didyme, et Nathanaël, celui de Cana en Galilée, et les [fils] de Zébédée, et deux autres de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.B: Simon Pierre se trouvait là avec Thomas (appelé Didyme, ce qui veut dire Jumeau), Nathanaël de Cana en Galilée, les fils de Zébédée et deux autres de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.R: Quelques disciples étaient ensemble. Il y avait Simon Pierre, et Thomas, qu’on appelait le Jumeau. Il y avait aussi Nathanaël, qui venait du village de Cana en Galilée. Les fils de Zébédée étaient là, et deux autres disciples de Jésus.

vi.L: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ, Thô-ma người được gọi là Đi-đim, Na-tha-na-ên người Ca-na xứ Ga-li-lê, [các con trai] của Xê-bê-đê và hai người khác trong các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang ở cùng nhau.
vi.B: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ đang ở đó cùng với Thô-ma (cũng gọi là Đi-đim, nghĩa là "Sinh Đôi"), Na-tha-na-ên người Ca-na xứ Ga-li-lê, các con trai của Xê-bê-đê và hai môn đồ khác của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Có mấy môn đồ đang ở cùng nhau. Đó là Si-môn Phi-e-rơ và Thô-ma, người được gọi là Sinh Đôi. Na-tha-na-ên cũng có mặt. Ông là người làng Ca-na thuộc miền Ga-li-lê. Các con trai của Xê-bê-đê cũng ở đó, cùng với hai môn đồ khác của Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 시몬 베드로와, 디두모라고 불리는 도마와, 갈릴리 가나 출신인 나다나엘과, 세베대의 [아들들]과, 그분의 제자들 가운데 다른 두 사람이 함께 있었다.
ko.B: 시몬 베드로와 함께, 쌍둥이라는 뜻의 디두모라고도 불리는 도마, 갈릴리 가나 출신 나다나엘, 세베대의 아들들, 그리고 예수의 다른 제자 두 사람이 있었다.
ko.R: 제자들 몇 사람이 함께 있었다. 시몬 베드로와, 쌍둥이라고 불리던 도마가 있었다. 나다나엘도 있었는데, 그는 갈릴리 지방 가나 마을 사람이었다. 세베대의 아들들도 있었고, 예수의 다른 제자 두 사람도 있었다.

decisions.choice: Thomas called Didymus: both names mean "twin"
decisions.reason: As at 11:16 and 20:24, John gives the Greek word for Thomas's Semitic name. Thomas is the disciple who confessed "My Lord and my God" a week after the resurrection (20:28).

decisions.choice: Nathanael from Cana: the disciple Jesus met in 1:45-51
decisions.reason: Nathanael appears only here and in 1:45-51, where Jesus saw him under the fig tree and Nathanael called him the Son of God and the King of Israel. Only here does John say that he came from Cana, the village where Jesus did his first sign (2:1, 11) and healed the official's son from afar (4:46-54).

decisions.choice: the ones of Zebedee: the sons of Zebedee, James and John
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "the ones of Zebedee", the usual way of naming a man's sons. The other Gospels name them as James and John, fishermen on this lake (Mark 1:19-20; Matthew 4:21). This is the only time John mentions them, and he never gives their names.

decisions.choice: two others of his disciples: two more disciples, not named
decisions.reason: With these two the group comes to seven. John does not say who the two were or whether they were among the Twelve. The disciple whom Jesus loved (verse 7) must be one of the seven, but John does not say which.

decisions.choice: [sons] of Zebedee (L); Zebedee's sons (B); The sons of Zebedee (R)
decisions.reason: English needs a noun where the Greek has only the article (meaning decision m3); Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: called Didymus, which means Twin (B); called the Twin (R); the town of Cana (R); disciples of Jesus (R)
decisions.reason: As at 11:16 and 20:24, Balanced adds what the name means and Readable gives only the meaning. Readable says that Cana was a town, breaks the list into short sentences and names Jesus for "his".

decisions.choice: le village de Cana
decisions.reason: Readable says what Cana was, as the English Readable does; French "ville" would make it sound larger than the village it was (meaning decision m2), as with Nazareth at 1:46.

decisions.choice: the list of names first, then "đang ở cùng nhau"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot open with "were together" before so long a subject; the verb is moved to the end.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς Σίμων Πέτρος· Ὑπάγω ἁλιεύειν· λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἐρχόμεθα καὶ ἡμεῖς σὺν σοί.

records.literal_gloss: Says to them Simon Peter: I am going away to fish; they say to him: Are coming also we with you.

en.L: Simon Peter says to them, "I am going off to fish." They say to him, "We also are coming with you."
en.B: Simon Peter said to them, "I am going out fishing." They answered, "We will come with you."
en.R: Simon Peter told the others, "I am going out to fish." They said, "We will come with you."

fr.L: Simon Pierre leur dit : « Je m’en vais pêcher. » Ils lui disent : « Nous venons, nous aussi, avec toi. »
fr.B: Simon Pierre leur dit : « Je vais pêcher. » Ils lui répondirent : « Nous venons avec toi. »
fr.R: Simon Pierre a dit aux autres : « Je vais pêcher. » Ils lui ont répondu : « Nous venons avec toi. »

vi.L: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ nói với họ: "Tôi đi đánh cá." Họ nói với ông: "Chúng tôi cũng đi với anh."
vi.B: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ bảo họ: "Tôi đi đánh cá đây." Họ đáp: "Chúng tôi cùng đi với anh."
vi.R: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ nói với các bạn: "Tôi đi đánh cá đây." Họ nói: "Chúng tôi sẽ đi với anh."

ko.L: 시몬 베드로가 그들에게 말한다. "나는 고기 잡으러 간다." 그들이 그에게 말한다. "우리도 너와 함께 간다."
ko.B: 시몬 베드로가 그들에게 "나는 고기를 잡으러 가겠다." 하고 말하자, 그들이 "우리도 함께 가겠다." 하고 대답했다.
ko.R: 시몬 베드로가 다른 제자들에게 말했다. "나는 물고기 잡으러 간다." 그러자 그들이 말했다. "우리도 같이 가겠다."

decisions.choice: I am going to fish: Peter goes back to the lake, and John does not say why
alternatives: Peter gives up his calling and returns to his old trade
a night's work to earn food
decisions.reason: The other Gospels tell that Peter and Andrew were fishermen on this lake when Jesus called them (Mark 1:16-18; Luke 5:1-11), and that the disciples were told to go to Galilee to meet the risen Jesus (Matthew 28:7, 10; Mark 16:7). John gives no reason for the fishing trip and makes no judgment on it. The story that follows turns on what they catch without Jesus and what they catch at his word.

decisions.choice: We also are coming: the other six go with Peter at once
decisions.reason: The present tense states a decision being carried out now. "They" are the other disciples named in verse 2; Peter leads and they follow.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal ("says", "see", "comes", "takes", "gives"); past tense at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John, Literal keeps the present tense with which John tells some past events ("says" in 21:3, 5, 7, 10, 12; "see" in 21:9; "comes", "takes" and "gives" in 21:13), which makes the story vivid. Balanced and Readable use the past, as English tells a story. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: going out fishing (B); going out to fish (R); We will come with you (B, R); told the others (R)
alternatives: I am going off to fish; We also are coming with you (Literal)
decisions.reason: English uses "will" for a decision made on the spot, where Greek can use the present (meaning decision m2). Readable says who "them" are.

decisions.choice: Nous venons avec toi (present, every level)
decisions.reason: French, like Greek, uses the present for a decision carried out on the spot (meaning decision m2), so every level keeps it where the English Balanced and Readable need "will".

decisions.choice: the disciples speak to one another as "tôi", "anh", "chúng tôi"
decisions.reason: Ordinary adult peers in the style guide's forms (section 6); neither intimate nor formal.

decisions.choice: historic present: plain "nói" with no "đã" at Literal; "bảo", "đáp" at Balanced
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has no tense; Literal leaves out the past marker for the Greek present, as the style guide sets, throughout this passage.

decisions.choice: historic present "말한다", "본다", "오신다" (L); past tense (B, R), through 21:1-14
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present in narrative; Balanced and Readable use the past. One decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: the disciples speak to each other in 해라체; "너와 함께" (L), "함께" / "같이" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The disciples are equals (style guide, section 4). Korean friends rarely say "you" to each other, so Balanced and Readable leave it out; Literal keeps it.

source.text: ἐξῆλθον καὶ ἐνέβησαν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον, καὶ ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἐπίασαν οὐδέν.

records.literal_gloss: They went out and got into the boat, and in that the night they caught nothing.

en.L: They went out and got into the boat, and during that night they caught nothing.
en.B: They went out and got into the boat, but all that night they caught nothing.
en.R: So they went off and climbed into the boat. But that whole night they did not catch anything.

fr.L: Ils sortirent et montèrent dans la barque, et cette nuit-là ils ne prirent rien.
fr.B: Ils sortirent et montèrent dans la barque, mais de toute cette nuit-là ils ne prirent rien.
fr.R: Ils sont donc partis et ils sont montés dans la barque. Mais pendant toute cette nuit, ils n’ont rien attrapé.

vi.L: Họ đi ra và xuống thuyền, và trong đêm ấy họ không bắt được gì cả.
vi.B: Họ ra đi và xuống thuyền, nhưng suốt đêm ấy chẳng bắt được con cá nào.
vi.R: Vậy họ đi ra và bước xuống thuyền. Nhưng suốt cả đêm đó, họ không bắt được con cá nào.

ko.L: 그들이 나가서 배에 올랐다. 그리고 그날 밤에 그들은 아무것도 잡지 못했다.
ko.B: 그들은 나가서 배를 탔지만, 그날 밤새도록 아무것도 잡지 못했다.
ko.R: 그들은 바닷가로 나가 배에 올라탔다. 그러나 그날 밤이 새도록 물고기를 한 마리도 잡지 못했다.

decisions.choice: that night: fishing with nets was done at night
decisions.reason: Fishermen on the lake worked through the night, when the fish come nearer the surface and do not see the nets, and brought in their catch at dawn (Luke 5:5, "we worked hard all night").

decisions.choice: they caught nothing: a whole night's work without result, before a great catch at Jesus's word
alternatives: no echo of the earlier story
decisions.reason: Luke tells of another night when Peter caught nothing, and of a great catch when he let down the nets at Jesus's word (Luke 5:4-7). John does not mention that story, but readers who knew it may hear it again here, after the resurrection. Jesus had said, "apart from me you can do nothing" (15:5).

decisions.choice: but all that night (B); But that whole night (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek joins the clauses with "and", but the sense is a contrast: they went out to fish and caught nothing. "All" or "whole" says what "that night" implies, that they fished the night through.

decisions.choice: "xuống thuyền" for "got into the boat"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese idiom: one goes "down" into a boat from the shore.

source.text: Πρωΐας δὲ ἤδη γενομένης ἔστη Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν· οὐ μέντοι ᾔδεισαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Early morning now already having come stood Jesus on the shore; not however knew the disciples that Jesus it is.

en.L: Now when early morning had already come, Jesus stood on the shore; the disciples, however, did not know that it was Jesus.
en.B: Just as day was breaking, Jesus stood on the shore, though the disciples did not realize that it was Jesus.
en.R: When morning came, Jesus was standing on the shore. But the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.

fr.L: Comme le matin était déjà venu, Jésus se tint sur le rivage ; les disciples, cependant, ne savaient pas que c’était Jésus.
fr.B: Le jour se levait déjà quand Jésus se tint sur le rivage ; mais les disciples ne savaient pas que c’était Jésus.
fr.R: Quand le matin est arrivé, Jésus était debout sur le rivage. Mais les disciples ne savaient pas que c’était Jésus.

vi.L: Khi trời đã sáng sớm, Đức Giê-xu đứng trên bờ; tuy nhiên các môn đồ không biết rằng đó là Đức Giê-xu.
vi.B: Vừa rạng sáng, Đức Giê-xu đứng trên bờ, nhưng các môn đồ không nhận ra đó là Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Khi trời sáng, Đức Giê-xu đứng trên bờ. Nhưng các môn đồ không biết đó là Đức Giê-xu.

ko.L: 벌써 이른 아침이 되었을 때 예수께서 바닷가에 서 계셨다. 그러나 제자들은 그분이 예수이신 줄 알지 못했다.
ko.B: 동이 틀 무렵 예수께서 물가에 서 계셨으나, 제자들은 그분이 예수이신 줄 알아보지 못했다.
ko.R: 아침이 밝아 올 때 예수께서 물가에 서 계셨다. 그러나 제자들은 그분이 예수이신 줄 몰랐다.

decisions.choice: early morning: first light, at the end of the night
decisions.reason: The word means the early part of the morning, and "already" sets it just after the night of verse 3. It is the time when fishermen came in with their catch. John marked the same early hour when Mary came to the tomb (20:1).

decisions.choice: did not know that it was Jesus: the risen Jesus is not recognized until he makes himself known
alternatives: only because of the distance and the poor light
decisions.reason: The boat was about a hundred yards out (verse 8) and the light was dim, which may be enough to explain it. But Mary Magdalene also did not know him at first, close at hand (20:14), and the two on the road to Emmaus did not either (Luke 24:16). John does not give the reason; he tells how they came to know him.

decisions.choice: however: a sharp contrast; that it is: the present tense of their thought
decisions.reason: The word for "however" sets what the disciples did not know against the fact that Jesus was there. In reporting what they did not know, Greek keeps the tense of the thought itself: "that it is Jesus".

decisions.choice: Just as day was breaking (B); When morning came (R); realize (B)
alternatives: when early morning had already come (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the time in everyday words. Every level reports the thought "it is Jesus" in the past, "it was Jesus", as English does (meaning decision m3). Balanced says "realize" for "know", since the disciples could see the man but did not know who he was.

decisions.choice: que c'était Jésus (every level)
decisions.reason: French reports a past thought in the imperfect ("ils ne savaient pas que c'était"), so no level keeps the Greek present of the thought (meaning decision m3).

source.text: λέγει οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Παιδία, μή τι προσφάγιον ἔχετε;

records.literal_gloss: Says therefore to them the Jesus: Children, not anything to-eat-with-bread do you have?

en.L: So Jesus says to them, "Children, you do not have anything to eat, do you?"
en.B: So Jesus called out to them, "Friends, you have no fish to eat, have you?"
en.R: Jesus called out to them, "Friends, you do not have any fish, do you?"

fr.L: Jésus leur dit donc : « Enfants, vous n’avez rien à manger ? »
fr.B: Jésus leur cria donc : « Les enfants, vous n’avez pas de poisson à manger ? »
fr.R: Jésus leur a crié : « Les amis, vous n’avez pas de poisson ? »

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hỡi các con, các con không có gì để ăn, phải không?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu gọi họ: "Này các con, các con không có cá để ăn, phải không?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu gọi lớn: "Các con ơi, các con chưa có cá phải không?"

ko.L: 그러므로 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하신다. "얘들아, 너희에게 먹을 것이 아무것도 없지 않느냐?"
ko.B: 그래서 예수께서 그들에게 소리쳐 물으셨다. "얘들아, 먹을 고기가 하나도 없느냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 그들을 부르셨다. "얘들아, 물고기를 하나도 못 잡았지?"

decisions.choice: Children: a friendly, familiar way to call to a group of men
alternatives: little children, a teacher's tender address to his own disciples
decisions.reason: The word means "children", but it was also used in everyday speech to call out to young men or workmen, much like "lads". The disciples do not yet know who is speaking (verse 4), so to them it sounds like a friendly call from a stranger on the shore. When Jesus spoke tenderly to his disciples at the supper, John used a different word (13:33).

decisions.choice: anything to eat: something to eat with bread, usually fish
decisions.reason: The word means a relish or side dish eaten with bread, the main food of every meal. By the lake that was nearly always fish (compare 6:9, small fish with barley loaves). The question asks whether they have caught anything.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no"
decisions.reason: The Greek negative in the question shows that the speaker expects "no". He seems to know that they have nothing.

decisions.choice: Friends (B, R)
decisions.reason: Spoken to grown men, "children" sounds odd or belittling in English; "friends" gives the friendly tone of the address (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: you do not have anything to eat, do you? (L); you have no fish to eat, have you? (B); you do not have any fish, do you? (R); called out (B, R)
decisions.reason: A question ending "do you?" or "have you?" shows that the answer "no" is expected (meaning decision m3). Balanced and Readable say "fish", which is what the word meant here (m2), and "called out", since he speaks from the shore to men in a boat.

decisions.choice: Enfants (L); Les enfants (B); Les amis (R)
decisions.reason: The word was a friendly call to a group of men (meaning decision m1). French "Les enfants !" is still said in this way to a group of adults, as a familiar call, so Balanced can keep the word; "Mes enfants" would sound like a father or a teacher, and "Les gars" is slang. Readable says "Les amis", as the English does, because young readers would take "les enfants" literally.

decisions.choice: vous n'avez rien à manger ? (L); vous n'avez pas de poisson ... ? (B, R)
alternatives: vous n'avez rien à manger, n'est-ce pas ?
decisions.reason: A French question in the negative already shows that the speaker expects "no" (meaning decision m3), so no level needs a tag like "n'est-ce pas". Balanced and Readable say "poisson", what the word meant here (m2).

decisions.choice: "các con" for paidia at every level ("Hỡi các con" L; "Này các con" B; "Các con ơi" R)
decisions.reason: Unlike English, where "Children" sounds odd and Balanced says "Friends", Vietnamese "các con" is the natural warm way an older man calls to younger men, and it is also how Jesus addresses his disciples elsewhere.

decisions.choice: "얘들아" at every level
decisions.reason: "얘들아" is the warm, familiar call an older man gives a group of younger men, close to the Greek "children" as the meaning decision reads it; "친구들" sounds translated and "여보게들" is old-fashioned. A reviewer should judge whether it sounds too much like speaking to boys.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ· Οὔ.

records.literal_gloss: They answered him: No.

en.L: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "No."
en.B: They answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "No."
en.R: "No, we do not," they answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondirent : « Non. »
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondirent : « Non. »
fr.R: « Non, nous n’en avons pas », {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont-ils répondu.

vi.L: Họ trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Không."
vi.B: Họ trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa không."
vi.R: "Dạ, không có," họ trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그들이 그분께 대답했다. "없습니다."
ko.B: 그들이 대답했다. "없습니다."
ko.R: "한 마리도 못 잡았습니다." 하고 그들이 대답했다.

decisions.choice: No: a flat answer, as the question expected
decisions.reason: The one-word answer confirms what the question assumed: after a whole night they have nothing (verse 3).

decisions.choice: answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: The disciples do not yet know that the man is Jesus (verse 4), but the pronoun refers to him, so it takes the reader setting for pronouns for God and Christ.

decisions.choice: No, we do not
decisions.reason: Readable completes the short answer, as English speakers would.

decisions.choice: "Thưa không" (B); "Dạ, không có" (R)
decisions.reason: A bare "Không" sounds curt to a stranger on the shore; "thưa" and "dạ" are the polite answer words Vietnamese requires. Literal keeps the bare word.

decisions.choice: the disciples answer the stranger in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Grown men answering a man they do not yet recognise on the shore use the formal style; it also matches how disciples speak to Jesus through the book (style guide, section 4).

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Βάλετε εἰς τὰ δεξιὰ μέρη τοῦ πλοίου τὸ δίκτυον, καὶ εὑρήσετε.

records.literal_gloss: He now said to them: Cast into the right parts of the boat the net, and you will find.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find [some]."
en.B: He said to them, "Throw the net out on the boat's right side, and you will find fish."
en.R: He told them, "Throw your net out on the right side of the boat. Then you will catch some fish."

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Jetez le filet du côté droit de la barque, et vous [en] trouverez. »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Jetez le filet du côté droit de la barque, et vous trouverez du poisson. »
fr.R: Il leur a dit : « Jetez votre filet du côté droit de la barque. Alors vous attraperez du poisson. »

vi.L: Ngài nói với họ: "Hãy thả lưới bên phải thuyền, thì các con sẽ tìm được [cá]."
vi.B: Ngài bảo họ: "Hãy thả lưới xuống bên phải thuyền, các con sẽ được cá."
vi.R: Ngài bảo họ: "Hãy thả lưới của các con xuống phía bên phải thuyền. Rồi các con sẽ bắt được cá."

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "배 오른쪽에 그물을 던져라. 그러면 [고기를] 찾을 것이다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "배 오른쪽으로 그물을 던져라. 그러면 고기가 잡힐 것이다."
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "배 오른쪽에 그물을 던져 보아라. 그러면 물고기를 잡을 것이다."

decisions.choice: the right side of the boat: simply the other side from where they had been fishing
alternatives: the side of favor or blessing
decisions.reason: In Scripture the right hand is often the side of honor (Psalm 110:1), and some readers have seen that here. The story gives no such hint: the point is that the catch comes when they do what Jesus says.

decisions.choice: you will find: a promise, with the object understood
decisions.reason: The verb has no object; from the question in verse 5 it is plain that fish are meant. The disciples obey a man they have not recognized, and the promise comes true at once.

decisions.choice: the net: a large fishing net let down from the boat
alternatives: a small cast net thrown by hand
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a fishing net. This one was big enough to hold 153 large fish (verse 11) and too heavy for the crew to haul aboard (verse 6), so it was a large net worked from the boat.

decisions.choice: Throw ... out (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Cast" is the fisherman's word, but in everyday English "throw out" is plainer. Literal keeps "cast", because the same verb returns in the next sentence and in verse 7, where Peter "cast himself" into the sea.

decisions.choice: [some] (L); fish (B); catch some fish (R); your net (R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object for "find" (meaning decision m2). Readable says what they will find and uses the everyday "catch".

decisions.choice: Jetez (every level)
decisions.reason: "Jeter le filet" is the ordinary French for casting a net, and the same verb serves when Peter "se jeta" into the sea in verse 7, so every level keeps the one verb, as the English Literal keeps "cast".

source.text: ἔβαλον οὖν, καὶ οὐκέτι αὐτὸ ἑλκύσαι ἴσχυον ἀπὸ τοῦ πλήθους τῶν ἰχθύων.

records.literal_gloss: They cast therefore, and no longer it to haul were they able from the multitude of the fish.

en.L: So they cast [it], and they were no longer able to haul it in because of the great number of fish.
en.B: So they threw it out, and now they could not haul it in because there were so many fish.
en.R: So they did. Then there were so many fish in the net that they were not able to pull it in.

fr.L: Ils [le] jetèrent donc, et ils n’avaient plus la force de le tirer, à cause de la quantité des poissons.
fr.B: Ils le jetèrent donc, et maintenant ils ne pouvaient plus le tirer, tant il y avait de poissons.
fr.R: C’est ce qu’ils ont fait. Alors il y a eu tellement de poissons dans le filet qu’ils n’arrivaient plus à le tirer.

vi.L: Vậy họ thả [lưới] xuống, và không còn kéo lưới lên nổi vì có quá nhiều cá.
vi.B: Họ thả lưới xuống, và giờ thì không kéo lên nổi vì cá quá nhiều.
vi.R: Họ làm theo. Bấy giờ cá vào lưới nhiều đến nỗi họ không kéo lưới lên được.

ko.L: 그래서 그들이 [그물을] 던졌더니, 고기가 너무 많아서 더 이상 그것을 끌어 올릴 수 없었다.
ko.B: 그래서 그들이 그물을 던졌는데, 고기가 너무 많이 걸려서 이제는 그물을 끌어 올릴 수가 없었다.
ko.R: 그들이 그렇게 하자, 그물에 물고기가 너무 많이 걸려서 그물을 끌어 올릴 수 없었다.

decisions.choice: haul: drag a heavy load, with a possible echo of Jesus drawing people to himself
alternatives: an ordinary word for hauling a net, with no echo
decisions.reason: The verb means to drag or pull something heavy; Peter uses it again in verse 11. John also uses it for the Father drawing people to Jesus (6:44) and for Jesus drawing all people to himself when he is lifted up (12:32). Some readers see the great catch as a picture of the people the disciples will bring in. John does not draw the link, and the word is the normal one for hauling a net.

decisions.choice: no longer able: now they could not, though the net had been light all night
decisions.reason: "No longer" sets the moment against the empty night before: suddenly the net is too heavy to haul. The tense pictures them trying and failing.

decisions.choice: because of the great number of fish
decisions.reason: The preposition gives the cause: the weight of so many fish.

decisions.choice: haul ... in (L, B); pull ... in (R)
decisions.reason: "Draw" is old-fashioned for a net. Literal and Balanced use "haul" here and in verse 11, so the repeated verb stays visible; Readable uses the plainer "pull" in both places.

decisions.choice: cast [it] (L); threw it out (B); So they did (R)
decisions.reason: The net is understood as the object; Literal brackets it. Readable says simply that they obeyed.

decisions.choice: tirer (every level, here and in verse 11)
decisions.reason: "Tirer" is the everyday verb for pulling a heavy load, so every level can use it here and when Peter hauls the net ashore in verse 11, keeping the repeated verb visible (meaning decision m1). "Haler" is a sailor's word and "hisser" means lifting upward. The possible echo of 6:44 and 12:32 is only as faint in French as in Greek, since "attirer" there comes from the same verb.

source.text: λέγει οὖν ὁ μαθητὴς ἐκεῖνος ὃν ἠγάπα ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ὁ κύριός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Says therefore the disciple that whom loved the Jesus to the Peter: The Lord it is.

en.L: So that disciple whom Jesus loved says to Peter, "It is the Lord!"
en.B: Then that disciple whom Jesus loved told Peter, "It is the Lord!"
en.R: The disciple whom Jesus loved told Peter, "It is the Lord!"

fr.L: Ce disciple que Jésus aimait dit donc à Pierre : « C’est le Seigneur ! »
fr.B: Alors ce disciple que Jésus aimait dit à Pierre : « C’est le Seigneur ! »
fr.R: Le disciple que Jésus aimait a dit à Pierre : « C’est le Seigneur ! »

vi.L: Vậy môn đồ ấy, người mà Đức Giê-xu yêu, nói với Phi-e-rơ: "Đó là Chúa!"
vi.B: Bấy giờ môn đồ mà Đức Giê-xu yêu nói với Phi-e-rơ: "Đó là Chúa!"
vi.R: Môn đồ mà Đức Giê-xu yêu nói với Phi-e-rơ: "Chúa đó!"

ko.L: 그러므로 예수께서 사랑하시는 그 제자가 베드로에게 말한다. "주님이시다!"
ko.B: 그때 예수께서 사랑하시는 그 제자가 베드로에게 말했다. "주님이시다!"
ko.R: 예수께서 사랑하시는 제자가 베드로에게 말했다. "주님이시다!"

decisions.choice: the disciple whom Jesus loved: the unnamed disciple of 13:23, 19:26 and 20:2
decisions.reason: John never names him. He is one of the seven of verse 2, and 21:20-24 says that he is the disciple who wrote these things. As at the empty tomb (20:8), he is the first to see what has happened.

decisions.choice: So: the catch is what tells him who the stranger is
decisions.reason: The word "so" ties his recognition to the catch of verse 6: the great haul, after a night of nothing, at the word of the man on the shore, shows him that it is Jesus.

decisions.choice: the Lord: the risen Jesus
alternatives: the master, a title of respect only
decisions.reason: Since the resurrection the disciples speak of Jesus as "the Lord" (20:18, 20, 25), the title Thomas gave him in his confession (20:28).

decisions.choice: It is the Lord!
alternatives: The Lord it is (word for word)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the exact words, as a cry of recognition; the Greek puts "the Lord" first for emphasis, which the exclamation mark carries in English. "The disciple whom Jesus loved" stays the same at every level (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: "môn đồ mà Đức Giê-xu yêu"
alternatives: "môn đồ được Đức Giê-xu yêu thương"
decisions.reason: The book-wide phrase for the beloved disciple, never named; "yêu" is the same verb used for both Greek verbs of love in 21:15-17.

decisions.choice: "예수께서 사랑하시는 제자" at every level, as everywhere in John
decisions.reason: The phrase is the disciple's fixed designation through the book (docs/john-terms.md). The present form "사랑하시는" reads as a standing title; "사랑하시던" could suggest a love that has ended.

source.text: Σίμων οὖν Πέτρος, ἀκούσας ὅτι ὁ κύριός ἐστιν, τὸν ἐπενδύτην διεζώσατο, ἦν γὰρ γυμνός, καὶ ἔβαλεν ἑαυτὸν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν·

records.literal_gloss: Simon therefore Peter, having heard that the Lord it is, the outer garment tied around himself, he was for stripped, and cast himself into the sea;

en.L: So Simon Peter, having heard that it was the Lord, tied the outer garment around [himself], for he was stripped [for work], and cast himself into the sea.
en.B: Hearing that it was the Lord, Simon Peter tied his outer garment around himself, since he had stripped for work, and threw himself into the sea.
en.R: When Simon Peter heard it was the Lord, he put on his outer coat and tied it, because he had taken it off to work. Then he jumped into the lake.

fr.L: Simon Pierre donc, ayant entendu que c’était le Seigneur, se ceignit de son vêtement de dessus, car il était dévêtu [pour le travail], et il se jeta dans la mer.
fr.B: Apprenant que c’était le Seigneur, Simon Pierre attacha son vêtement de dessus autour de lui, car il s’était mis en tenue légère pour travailler, et il se jeta à la mer.
fr.R: Quand Simon Pierre a entendu que c’était le Seigneur, il a remis son manteau et il l’a attaché, parce qu’il l’avait enlevé pour travailler. Puis il a sauté dans le lac.

vi.L: Vậy Si-môn Phi-e-rơ, khi nghe rằng đó là Chúa, liền thắt áo ngoài vào, vì ông đang cởi trần [để làm việc], và lao mình xuống biển.
vi.B: Nghe nói đó là Chúa, Si-môn Phi-e-rơ khoác áo ngoài vào và thắt lại, vì ông đã cởi áo ra để làm việc, rồi lao mình xuống biển.
vi.R: Khi Si-môn Phi-e-rơ nghe đó là Chúa, ông mặc áo ngoài vào và thắt dây lại, vì ông đã cởi áo ra để làm việc. Rồi ông nhảy xuống nước.

ko.L: 그러므로 시몬 베드로는 주님이시라는 말을 듣고 겉옷을 몸에 두르고 띠를 매었다. 그가 [일하느라 겉옷을] 벗고 있었기 때문이다. 그리고 자기 몸을 바다에 던졌다.
ko.B: 시몬 베드로는 주님이시라는 말을 듣자, 일하느라 벗어 두었던 겉옷을 걸치고 허리띠를 맨 다음 바다로 뛰어들었다.
ko.R: 시몬 베드로는 주님이시라는 말을 듣고 겉옷을 입고 허리띠를 맸다. 일을 하느라 겉옷을 벗어 두었던 것이다. 그러고는 호수로 뛰어들었다.

decisions.choice: stripped: lightly dressed for work, not necessarily naked
decisions.reason: The word means "naked", but it was also used of someone wearing only a short tunic or loincloth without an outer garment, as a man doing hard work might be. That is the natural picture for a fisherman at work in a boat. A footnote gives "naked".

decisions.choice: tied his outer garment around himself: put it on and belted it
alternatives: tucked up the clothing he was wearing
decisions.reason: The verb means to tie something around oneself; John used it of Jesus tying the towel around himself at the supper (13:4-5). It seems strange to put on more clothing before going into the water, but a Jew would not come before another person, least of all the Lord, without proper clothes, and a belted garment would not hinder him in the water. The exact action is not certain.

decisions.choice: threw himself into the sea: to reach Jesus ahead of the boat
decisions.reason: John does not say whether Peter swam or waded. The boat was about a hundred yards out (verse 8), and Peter does not wait for it. It is the same verb as "cast" the net in verse 6.

decisions.choice: stripped [for work] (L); had stripped for work (B); had taken it off to work (R)
decisions.reason: In English "naked" means wearing nothing, which is more than the Greek word need mean here (meaning decision m1). Literal brackets "for work", which the context supplies.

decisions.choice: his outer garment (B); put on his outer coat and tied it (R); threw himself (B); jumped (R); the lake (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday verbs. Readable spells out putting the coat on and tying it (meaning decision m2), and says "lake" for the sea, as it does in chapter 6.

decisions.choice: dévêtu [pour le travail] (L); en tenue légère pour travailler (B); il l'avait enlevé pour travailler (R)
decisions.reason: French "nu" means wearing nothing, which is more than the Greek word need mean here (meaning decision m1, whose footnote gives "naked"). "Dévêtu" says that he had taken his clothes off without saying that he wore nothing; Balanced and Readable say plainly that he was lightly dressed for work.

decisions.choice: se ceignit de son vêtement de dessus (L); attacha son vêtement de dessus autour de lui (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is to tie something around oneself, as in 13:4-5 (meaning decision m2). "Se ceindre de" says exactly that and is the word for tying on a belt or a towel; it is literary, so Balanced spells it out. Readable says he put his coat back on and tied it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "cởi trần [để làm việc]" (L); "đã cởi áo ra để làm việc" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "trần truồng" would say he was naked; "cởi trần" (bare to the waist) matches the meaning decision that he was lightly dressed for work.

decisions.choice: "[일하느라 겉옷을] 벗고 있었기" (L); "일하느라 벗어 두었던 겉옷" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean "벌거벗다" means wholly naked, which the meaning decision says is not necessarily meant; naming the outer garment and the work says what Peter had taken off.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἄλλοι μαθηταὶ τῷ πλοιαρίῳ ἦλθον, οὐ γὰρ ἦσαν μακρὰν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀλλὰ ὡς ἀπὸ πηχῶν διακοσίων, σύροντες τὸ δίκτυον τῶν ἰχθύων.

records.literal_gloss: The but other disciples in the little boat came, not for were they far from the land but about from cubits two hundred, dragging the net of the fish.

en.L: But the other disciples came in the little boat, for they were not far from the land, but about 200 cubits off, dragging the net of fish.
en.B: The other disciples came in the boat, towing the net full of fish. They were not far out, only about {{units:100 yards|200 cubits}} from land.
en.R: The other disciples came to shore in the boat, pulling the net full of fish behind them. They were not far from land, only about {{units:100 yards|200 cubits}}.

fr.L: Mais les autres disciples vinrent avec la petite barque, car ils n’étaient pas loin de la terre, mais à environ deux cents coudées, traînant le filet de poissons.
fr.B: Les autres disciples vinrent avec la barque, en traînant le filet plein de poissons ; ils n’étaient pas loin de la terre, à {{units:90 mètres|deux cents coudées}} environ.
fr.R: Les autres disciples sont revenus vers le rivage avec la barque, en tirant derrière eux le filet plein de poissons. Ils n’étaient pas loin de la terre, seulement à {{units:90 mètres|deux cents coudées}} environ.

vi.L: Còn các môn đồ khác đến bằng chiếc thuyền nhỏ, vì họ không xa đất liền, chỉ khoảng 200 cu-đê, [và] kéo theo lưới cá.
vi.B: Các môn đồ khác đi thuyền vào, kéo theo lưới đầy cá. Họ cách bờ không xa, chỉ chừng {{units:90 m|200 cu-đê}}.
vi.R: Các môn đồ khác chèo thuyền vào bờ, kéo theo sau lưới đầy cá. Họ không ở xa bờ lắm, chỉ khoảng {{units:90 m|200 cu-đê}}.

ko.L: 그러나 다른 제자들은 고기가 든 그물을 끌면서 작은 배를 타고 왔다. 그들이 육지에서 멀리 있지 않고, 이백 규빗쯤 떨어진 곳에 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 다른 제자들은 고기가 가득 든 그물을 끌면서 배를 타고 왔다. 그들은 육지에서 멀지 않은, {{units:90미터|이백 규빗}}쯤 떨어진 곳에 있었다.
ko.R: 다른 제자들은 물고기가 가득 찬 그물을 배 뒤에 매달아 끌면서 물가로 왔다. 육지에서 {{units:90미터|이백 규빗}}쯤밖에 떨어져 있지 않았기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: the little boat: the same boat as in verse 3
alternatives: a small boat towed behind the fishing boat
decisions.reason: The word is a smaller form of the word for boat in verse 3, but John uses the two words for the same boats in 6:17-24. Nothing suggests a second boat.

decisions.choice: about two hundred cubits: about 300 feet, or 100 yards
decisions.reason: A cubit, the length of a forearm, was about 18 inches (45 cm), so two hundred cubits is about 300 feet (90 meters). The boat was near enough to shore for a man to swim or wade, and for the crew to tow in a net they could not lift.

decisions.choice: dragging the net: towing the net, full of fish, through the water
decisions.reason: They could not haul the net into the boat (verse 6), so they dragged it along in the water as they came in. Peter later hauls it ashore (verse 11).

decisions.choice: about {{units:100 yards|200 cubits}}
decisions.reason: A cubit means little to most readers, so Balanced and Readable give the distance in yards by default, and the units setting shows the original measure (meaning decision m2). Literal always keeps the ancient unit. Numerals are used in measurements.

decisions.choice: the boat (B, R); towing (B); full of fish (B, R); only (B, R); to shore, behind them (R)
alternatives: the little boat; the net of fish (Literal)
decisions.reason: "The net of fish" means the net full of fish. "Only" brings out the contrast of "not far ... but about". Balanced and Readable say "the boat", since it is the boat of verse 3 (meaning decision m1). Readable says where they were going and how the net came with them (m3).

decisions.choice: à {{units:90 mètres|deux cents coudées}} environ
decisions.reason: French readers measure in metres, so the modern default is metric, not the yards of the English. A cubit was about 45 cm, so two hundred cubits is about 90 metres (meaning decision m2); "une centaine de mètres" would round it up. The units setting shows the original measure, which Literal always keeps.

decisions.choice: {{units:90 m|200 cu-đê}}; Literal "200 cu-đê"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese uses metric by default with the original unit as the alternative (style guide section 7), unlike the English; a cubit is about 45 cm. "cu-đê" is the established Vietnamese Bible word for the cubit.

decisions.choice: "이백 규빗" (L); {{units:90미터|이백 규빗}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Korean uses metric measures by default with the original unit as the alternative (style guide, section 7), unlike the English US units; a cubit is about 45 centimetres. "규빗" is the established Korean form of the unit. Literal keeps the original. The participle clause "dragging the net" is moved before the verb, as Korean word order requires.

source.text: Ὡς οὖν ἀπέβησαν εἰς τὴν γῆν βλέπουσιν ἀνθρακιὰν κειμένην καὶ ὀψάριον ἐπικείμενον καὶ ἄρτον.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore they got out onto the land they see a charcoal fire lying and fish lying on [it] and bread.

en.L: So when they got out onto the land, they see a charcoal fire set there, and fish lying on [it], and bread.
en.B: When they came ashore, they saw a charcoal fire already there, with fish laid on it, and bread.
en.R: When they got out of the boat on the shore, they saw a charcoal fire. There was fish cooking on it, and there was some bread.

fr.L: Quand donc ils furent descendus à terre, ils voient un feu de braises disposé là, et du poisson posé dessus, et du pain.
fr.B: Quand ils eurent débarqué, ils virent un feu de braises déjà allumé, avec du poisson posé dessus, et du pain.
fr.R: Quand ils sont descendus de la barque sur le rivage, ils ont vu un feu de braises. Du poisson cuisait dessus, et il y avait aussi du pain.

vi.L: Vậy khi họ lên bờ, họ thấy một đống lửa than đặt sẵn, có cá đặt trên [đó], và bánh.
vi.B: Khi lên bờ, họ thấy một bếp lửa than đã nhóm sẵn, trên đó có cá, và có cả bánh.
vi.R: Khi bước ra khỏi thuyền lên bờ, họ thấy một bếp lửa than. Trên lửa có cá đang nướng, và có cả bánh nữa.

ko.L: 그러므로 그들이 육지에 내렸을 때, 숯불이 피워져 있고 그 위에 생선이 놓여 있고 빵도 있는 것을 본다.
ko.B: 그들이 뭍에 올라와 보니, 숯불이 피워져 있고 그 위에 생선이 놓여 있었으며, 빵도 있었다.
ko.R: 그들이 배에서 내려 물가에 올라와 보니, 숯불이 피워져 있었다. 숯불 위에서는 생선이 구워지고 있었고, 빵도 있었다.

decisions.choice: a charcoal fire: the same word as in 18:18, where Peter denied Jesus
alternatives: no connection between the two scenes
decisions.reason: This word for a fire of glowing charcoal is used only twice in the New Testament: in 18:18, where Peter stood warming himself at a charcoal fire and denied Jesus three times, and here, before Jesus asks Peter three times whether he loves him (21:15-17). John may mean the reader to remember the first fire at the second. The link rests on one word, so it cannot be proved.

decisions.choice: fish lying on it: fish cooking on the coals, the same word as for the fish in 6:9-11
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the small fish eaten with bread at the feeding of the five thousand (6:9, 11). Jesus already has fish cooking before the disciples bring any of theirs. John does not say where it came from.

decisions.choice: fish ... bread: the Greek words are singular
decisions.reason: Both words are singular. They can mean a single fish and a single loaf, or fish and bread in general. John does not settle it, and verse 13 speaks of "the bread" and "the fish" in the same way.

decisions.choice: already there (B); cooking (R); saw (B, R)
alternatives: see a charcoal fire set there (Literal)
decisions.reason: The fire was laid and burning when they landed; Balanced brings this out with "already", and Readable says that the fish was cooking, which is what lying on the coals means. On "see" and "saw", see the historic present at verse 3. The words "fish" and "bread" can be singular or general in English, which keeps the question of meaning decision m3 open.

decisions.choice: un feu de braises; du poisson, du pain
alternatives: un feu de charbon de bois
decisions.reason: "Un feu de braises" is a fire of glowing coals, the sense of the word, in everyday French; the same words should render the same Greek word at 18:18, where Peter denied Jesus by such a fire, so that the echo meaning decision m1 points to stays visible (a reviewer should check 18:18). The partitive "du poisson", "du pain" leaves open, as the Greek singular does, whether one fish and one loaf are meant or fish and bread in general (m3).

decisions.choice: "lửa than" for anthrakia
decisions.reason: Keeps "than" (charcoal) so the link with the fire of Peter's denial in 18:18 can be seen; 18:18 should use the same words.

decisions.choice: "숯불" at every level, as in 18:18
decisions.reason: The same Greek word is used only here and at 18:18, where Peter denied Jesus by a charcoal fire; Korean keeps the same word in both places so the reader can hear the echo the meaning decision notes.

decisions.choice: "생선" for opsarion (fish as food, verses 9, 10, 13); "고기" / "물고기" for ichthys (the catch, verses 6, 8, 11)
decisions.reason: John uses two words: one for fish as something to eat with bread, one for the fish in the net. "생선" and "고기" keep the difference without strain; Readable uses "물고기" for fish just caught.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἐνέγκατε ἀπὸ τῶν ὀψαρίων ὧν ἐπιάσατε νῦν.

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Jesus: Bring from the fish which you caught now.

en.L: Jesus says to them, "Bring [some] of the fish which you have now caught."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Bring some of the fish that you have just caught."
en.R: Jesus told them, "Bring some of the fish you just caught."

fr.L: Jésus leur dit : « Apportez [quelques-uns] des poissons que vous avez pris à l’instant. »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Apportez quelques-uns des poissons que vous venez de prendre. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Apportez quelques-uns des poissons que vous venez d’attraper. »

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hãy đem [một ít] cá các con vừa bắt được."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo họ: "Hãy mang ít cá các con vừa bắt được đến đây."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu bảo họ: "Đem mấy con cá các con mới bắt được lại đây."

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하신다. "너희가 방금 잡은 생선 가운데서 [몇 마리를] 가져오너라."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "방금 잡은 생선을 몇 마리 가져오너라."
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "방금 잡은 물고기를 몇 마리 가져오너라."

decisions.choice: from the fish: some of them
decisions.reason: The preposition takes a part of the catch, not all of it.

decisions.choice: the fish you caught: their catch is added to the meal Jesus has made ready
decisions.reason: The word for fish is the same as in verse 9. Jesus already has fish on the fire, yet he asks for some of theirs, so that what they caught at his word is part of the meal. John does not explain the request.

decisions.choice: now: just now, this morning
decisions.reason: "Now" sets this catch against the empty night: these are the fish caught a moment ago at his word.

decisions.choice: [some] (L); some (B, R); have now caught (L); have just caught (B); just caught (R)
decisions.reason: English needs "some" to show the part taken (meaning decision m1); Literal brackets it. "Just" is the everyday English for "now" with a past action.

source.text: ἀνέβη οὖν Σίμων Πέτρος καὶ εἵλκυσεν τὸ δίκτυον εἰς τὴν γῆν μεστὸν ἰχθύων μεγάλων ἑκατὸν πεντήκοντα τριῶν· καὶ τοσούτων ὄντων οὐκ ἐσχίσθη τὸ δίκτυον.

records.literal_gloss: Went up therefore Simon Peter and hauled the net to the land, full of fish large, a hundred fifty three; and so many being not was torn the net.

en.L: So Simon Peter went up and hauled the net to the land, full of large fish, 153; and although there were so many, the net was not torn.
en.B: So Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net ashore, full of large fish, 153 of them. Even with so many, the net did not tear.
en.R: So Simon Peter climbed into the boat and pulled the net onto the shore. It was full of big fish, 153 of them. There were so many, but the net did not tear.

fr.L: Simon Pierre monta donc et tira le filet à terre, plein de gros poissons, 153 ; et alors qu’il y en avait tant, le filet ne se déchira pas.
fr.B: Simon Pierre monta donc dans la barque et tira le filet à terre, plein de gros poissons : 153. Malgré leur nombre, le filet ne se déchira pas.
fr.R: Alors Simon Pierre est monté dans la barque et il a tiré le filet sur le rivage. Il était plein de gros poissons, 153 en tout. Il y en avait beaucoup, mais le filet ne s’est pas déchiré.

vi.L: Vậy Si-môn Phi-e-rơ lên [thuyền] và kéo lưới vào bờ, đầy những cá lớn, một trăm năm mươi ba [con]; và dù có nhiều như thế, lưới vẫn không bị rách.
vi.B: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ bước lên thuyền và kéo lưới vào bờ, đầy những cá lớn, cả thảy một trăm năm mươi ba con. Dù nhiều như vậy mà lưới không bị rách.
vi.R: Si-môn Phi-e-rơ trèo lên thuyền và kéo lưới vào bờ. Lưới đầy cá lớn, tất cả một trăm năm mươi ba con. Cá nhiều như vậy mà lưới vẫn không rách.

ko.L: 그러므로 시몬 베드로가 올라가서 그물을 육지로 끌어 올렸는데, [그물에는] 큰 고기가 153마리나 가득했다. 그리고 그렇게 많았는데도 그물은 찢어지지 않았다.
ko.B: 시몬 베드로가 배에 올라가 그물을 뭍으로 끌어 올렸다. 그물에는 큰 고기가 가득했는데, 153마리나 되었다. 고기가 그렇게 많았는데도 그물은 찢어지지 않았다.
ko.R: 시몬 베드로가 배에 올라가서 그물을 물가로 끌어 올렸다. 그물에는 큰 물고기가 가득했는데, 모두 153마리였다. 그렇게 많았는데도 그물은 찢어지지 않았다.

decisions.choice: went up: climbed aboard the boat, which had come to shore
alternatives: went up the beach to where the net lay
decisions.reason: The verb is used for getting into a boat (Mark 6:51; Matthew 14:32), and Peter needs to be at the boat to haul out the net that the others had dragged in. The Greek does not say "into the boat", so the sense "went up the beach" is also possible.

decisions.choice: a hundred and fifty-three: the count of a real catch
alternatives: a number with a hidden meaning
decisions.reason: Fishermen counted a catch in order to share it out or sell it, and an exact number fits the memory of someone who was there (21:24). Readers have also looked for a meaning in the number: for example, that it stands for the whole range of peoples to be gathered in by the disciples' mission. It is the sum of all the numbers from 1 to 17, and the fishermen of Ezekiel 47:10 catch fish "of many kinds". John gives no hint that the number means more than the count.

decisions.choice: the net was not torn: so great a catch, and none lost
alternatives: a detail of the scene only
decisions.reason: The verb is the one the soldiers use of Jesus's seamless tunic, "Let us not tear it" (19:24), and the related noun is John's word for the divisions among people over Jesus (7:43; 9:16; 10:19). Some readers see the unbroken net as a picture of the one flock gathered by Jesus (10:16; 17:21). John says only that it held.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written in numerals at every level.

decisions.choice: went aboard (B); climbed into the boat (R); hauled (L, B); pulled (R); Even with so many, the net did not tear (B); There were so many, but (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where Peter went (meaning decision m1). "Hauled" and "pulled" repeat the verb of verse 6: what the crew could not do in the water, Peter now does on land. Readable makes the contrast its own sentence.

decisions.choice: "một trăm năm mươi ba" in words
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese style guide writes numbers in running text as words; the count is not a measure.

decisions.choice: "153마리" in figures at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide writes short numbers in words and larger ones in figures; figures make this exact count easy to read and to find.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Δεῦτε ἀριστήσατε.

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Jesus: Come, have breakfast.

en.L: Jesus says to them, "Come, have breakfast."
en.B: Jesus said to them, "Come, eat your breakfast."
en.R: Jesus said to them, "Come and eat breakfast."

fr.L: Jésus leur dit : « Venez, prenez le petit-déjeuner. »
fr.B: Jésus leur dit : « Venez prendre le petit-déjeuner. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a dit : « Venez prendre le petit-déjeuner. »

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Hãy đến ăn sáng."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo họ: "Hãy đến mà ăn sáng."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với họ: "Đến đây ăn sáng nào."

ko.L: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하신다. "와서 아침을 먹어라."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "와서 아침을 먹어라."
ko.R: 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "이리 와서 아침을 먹어라."

decisions.choice: have breakfast: eat the morning meal
decisions.reason: The verb means to eat the first meal of the day; it could also be used of a later meal, but here it is daybreak (verse 4) after a night on the water.

decisions.choice: Come: Jesus invites them as host
decisions.reason: The fire, the fish and the bread are his (verse 9), and he calls them to eat, as a host does. He then serves them himself (verse 13).

decisions.choice: eat your breakfast (B); eat breakfast (R); said (B, R)
decisions.reason: Everyday words for the invitation. On "says" and "said", see the historic present at verse 3.

decisions.choice: prendre le petit-déjeuner
decisions.reason: The verb means to eat the first meal of the day (meaning decision m1). French "déjeuner" is that meal in Belgium, Switzerland, Quebec and much of francophone Africa, but the midday meal in France, so it would be read two ways; "le petit-déjeuner" is understood everywhere as the morning meal.

source.text: οὐδεὶς δὲ ἐτόλμα τῶν μαθητῶν ἐξετάσαι αὐτόν· Σὺ τίς εἶ;

records.literal_gloss: None now dared of the disciples to question him: You who are?

en.L: But none of the disciples dared to question {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.B: Not one of the disciples dared ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.R: None of the disciples were brave enough to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

fr.L: Mais aucun des disciples n’osait {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}interroger : « Toi, qui es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? »
fr.B: Aucun des disciples n’osait {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander : « Qui es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? »
fr.R: Aucun des disciples n’avait le courage de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander : « Qui es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? »

vi.L: Nhưng không ai trong các môn đồ dám hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ngài là ai?"
vi.B: Không một môn đồ nào dám hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ngài là ai?"
vi.R: Không môn đồ nào đủ can đảm hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ngài là ai?"

ko.L: 그러나 제자들 가운데 아무도 감히 그분께 "선생님은 누구십니까?" 하고 캐어묻지 못했다.
ko.B: 제자들 가운데 누구도 감히 "선생님은 누구십니까?" 하고 그분께 묻지 못했다.
ko.R: 제자들 가운데 아무도 "선생님은 누구십니까?" 하고 여쭈어 볼 용기가 없었다.

decisions.choice: none dared to ask: they felt awe before the risen Jesus
alternatives: they were simply too shy to ask a stranger
decisions.reason: They knew who he was (the next sentence), yet something in him made them want to ask and kept them from asking. The risen Jesus is the same Jesus, but not always known at once (20:14; Luke 24:16, 31), and the disciples stand in awe of him.

decisions.choice: question: ask closely, inquire
decisions.reason: The verb means to examine or inquire carefully (Matthew 2:8; 10:11). They did not dare to question him about who he was.

decisions.choice: You, who are you?: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "you" first, as in the questions put to John the Baptist (1:19) and to Jesus himself (8:25).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?
decisions.reason: The question would be spoken to Jesus, so "you" as well as "him" takes the reader setting for pronouns for God and Christ.

decisions.choice: Not one ... dared ask (B); None ... were brave enough to ask (R)
decisions.reason: "Ask" is the plain English verb for a question; "not one" keeps the force of "none". Readable uses everyday words for "dared".

decisions.choice: "Ngài là ai?" with "Ngài" written plainly
decisions.reason: The pronoun opens the question, so by the style guide it is written plainly with its capital rather than as a deity_pronoun span. "Ngài" is the respectful "you" of awe the meaning decision describes.

decisions.choice: "선생님은 누구십니까?" for the stressed "You, who are you?"
decisions.reason: Korean marks the stressed "you" with a title, not a pronoun: "당신" would be rude to Jesus, and "주님" would already answer the question. "선생님" is the respectful address to a man whose identity is being asked.

source.text: εἰδότες ὅτι ὁ κύριός ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: knowing that the Lord it is.

en.L: [They were] knowing that it was the Lord.
en.B: They knew it was the Lord.
en.R: They knew that it was the Lord.

fr.L: Ils savaient que c’était le Seigneur.
fr.B: Car ils savaient que c’était le Seigneur.
fr.R: Ils savaient que c’était le Seigneur.

vi.L: [Vì họ] biết rằng đó là Chúa.
vi.B: Họ biết đó là Chúa.
vi.R: Họ biết rằng đó chính là Chúa.

ko.L: 주님이신 줄 알고 있었던 것이다.
ko.B: 그들은 그분이 주님이신 것을 알고 있었다.
ko.R: 그분이 주님이시라는 것을 모두 알고 있었기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: knowing: the reason they did not ask
alternatives: knowing, and yet wanting to ask
decisions.reason: The participle belongs with "none of the disciples dared" in the sentence before; the SBLGNT puts a stop between them, but the sense runs on. They did not ask because they already knew the answer; the urge to ask shows how strange the meeting was (meaning decision m1 on the sentence before).

decisions.choice: the Lord: the risen Jesus, as in verse 7
decisions.reason: What the disciple whom Jesus loved said in verse 7, "It is the Lord", all of them now know.

decisions.choice: [They were] knowing (L); They knew (B, R)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT makes these words a sentence of their own, so English needs a subject and a finite verb; Literal brackets what it supplies and keeps the participle.

decisions.choice: Ils savaient (L); Car ils savaient (B)
decisions.reason: French cannot make a sentence of a participle with a supplied "être", as the English Literal does, so Literal gives the participle as a plain verb. Balanced adds "car" to show that their knowing is why they did not ask (meaning decision m1), as the participle does in Greek.

source.text: ἔρχεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ λαμβάνει τὸν ἄρτον καὶ δίδωσιν αὐτοῖς, καὶ τὸ ὀψάριον ὁμοίως.

records.literal_gloss: Comes Jesus and takes the bread and gives to them, and the fish likewise.

en.L: Jesus comes and takes the bread and gives [it] to them, and the fish likewise.
en.B: Jesus came, took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish in the same way.
en.R: Jesus came over, took the bread, and gave it to them. He gave them the fish in the same way.

fr.L: Jésus vient, et il prend le pain et [le] leur donne, et le poisson de même.
fr.B: Jésus vint, prit le pain et le leur donna, et fit de même avec le poisson.
fr.R: Jésus est venu vers eux, il a pris le pain et il le leur a donné. Il leur a donné le poisson de la même façon.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đến, lấy bánh và đưa cho họ, cá cũng vậy.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đến, lấy bánh trao cho họ, rồi cá cũng thế.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu lại gần, lấy bánh và đưa cho họ. Ngài cũng đưa cá cho họ như vậy.

ko.L: 예수께서 오신다. 그리고 빵을 집어 그들에게 주시고, 생선도 마찬가지로 [주신다].
ko.B: 예수께서 다가오셔서 빵을 집어 그들에게 주시고, 생선도 그렇게 나누어 주셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 가까이 오셔서 빵을 집어 그들에게 주셨다. 생선도 똑같이 나누어 주셨다.

decisions.choice: takes the bread and gives it to them: an echo of the feeding by the same lake
alternatives: an ordinary host serving a meal, with no echo
decisions.reason: At the feeding of the five thousand, also by this lake, Jesus "took the loaves ... and distributed" them, "likewise also the fish" (6:11). Here he takes, gives, and does "likewise" with the fish. Readers may also think of the Lord's Supper, where Jesus took bread and gave it (Luke 22:19), though John does not mention a thanksgiving here. The words are also the plain way to describe a host serving a meal.

decisions.choice: the bread, the fish: the bread and fish already on the fire
decisions.reason: The article points back to the bread and fish of verse 9. Jesus serves them from what he has prepared.

decisions.choice: comes: Jesus comes over to them, by the fire
decisions.reason: John does not say where Jesus was standing; the verb shows him coming to where they were to serve them.

decisions.choice: came, took, gave (B, R); in the same way (B, R); came over (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense (see the historic present at verse 3) and the everyday "in the same way" for "likewise". Readable makes the fish a sentence of its own.

records.literal_gloss: This [was] already a third [time] was revealed the Jesus to the disciples having been raised out of dead.

en.L: This [was] now the third time Jesus was revealed to the disciples after being raised from [the] dead.
en.B: This was now the third time that Jesus was revealed to the disciples after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been raised from the dead.
en.R: This was the third time Jesus showed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} to the disciples after {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been raised from the dead.

fr.L: Ce [fut] déjà la troisième [fois] que Jésus fut manifesté aux disciples, relevé d’entre [les] morts.
fr.B: C’était déjà la troisième fois que Jésus se manifestait aux disciples depuis qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait été ressuscité d’entre les morts.
fr.R: C’était la troisième fois que Jésus se montrait aux disciples depuis qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait été ressuscité d’entre les morts.

vi.L: Đây [là] lần thứ ba Đức Giê-xu được tỏ ra cho các môn đồ, sau khi được làm cho sống lại từ [cõi] chết.
vi.B: Đó là lần thứ ba Đức Giê-xu tỏ mình ra cho các môn đồ sau khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được làm cho sống lại từ cõi chết.
vi.R: Đây là lần thứ ba Đức Giê-xu hiện ra cho các môn đồ thấy sau khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} được sống lại từ cõi chết.

ko.L: 이것은 예수께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살리심을 받으신 뒤에, 벌써 세 번째로 제자들에게 나타나신 것이었다.
ko.B: 이것은 예수께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 살아나신 뒤에 제자들에게 나타나신 것으로, 이번이 벌써 세 번째였다.
ko.R: 이렇게 예수께서 죽었다가 다시 살아나신 뒤에 제자들에게 모습을 보이신 것은 이번이 세 번째였다.

decisions.choice: the third time: the third appearance to the disciples as a group
alternatives: the third appearance of any kind
decisions.reason: John has told of two appearances to the disciples together: on the evening of the first day (20:19-23) and a week later with Thomas (20:26-29). This is the third. The appearance to Mary Magdalene alone (20:14-18) is not counted among appearances "to the disciples".

decisions.choice: was revealed: the same verb as in verse 1, closing the story
decisions.reason: Verse 1 opened with "Jesus revealed himself"; this verse closes with "Jesus was revealed". The passive keeps the sense of something made known, not just seen.

decisions.choice: after being raised from the dead: raised by God
alternatives: after rising from the dead by his own act
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, the usual way of saying that God raised Jesus (as in 2:22, "when he was raised from the dead"). John also records Jesus saying that he has authority to take his life up again (10:17-18); the two belong together.

decisions.choice: was revealed (B); showed himself (R); after he had been raised (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "revealed" to match verse 1; Readable says "showed himself", as in verse 1. Balanced and Readable turn the participle into a clause with "he".

decisions.choice: fut manifesté (L); se manifestait (B); se montrait (R); relevé (L); avait été ressuscité (B, R)
decisions.reason: The passive of "manifester" is stiff in French outside Literal; the reflexive "se manifestait" matches "se manifesta" in verse 1, which this verse answers (meaning decision m2). For "raised", Literal says "relevé" and Balanced and Readable "ressuscité", as at 2:22; all keep the passive, since "il était ressuscité" would read as his own act rather than God raising him (m3).

decisions.choice: "tỏ mình ra" (B), "hiện ra" (R) for the passive "was revealed"; Literal keeps "được tỏ ra"
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese passive "được tỏ ra" is stiff; the active reflexive says the same thing and matches verse 1.

decisions.choice: "살리심을 받으신" (L); "살아나신" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is passive, raised by God; "살리심을 받다" keeps the passive with the honorific at Literal. Balanced and Readable use the ordinary Korean "살아나다".
